structure.overview: The case concerns the appellant Gérard Dugré's appeals against three Federal Court decisions dismissing his motions to stay a Canadian Judicial Council inquiry. The Attorney General, as respondent, argued the appeals should be dismissed due to lack of a main proceeding and failure to meet stay criteria. The Federal Court of Appeal dismissed the appeals as doomed to fail and refused to stay the appeals, citing procedural congestion and prior decisions.

party_points.text: appeals should be dismissed for no main proceeding and lack of stay criteria
seeks stay of appeals pending Supreme Court leave or decision on Dugré #1

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The appellant Gérard Dugré appeals three Federal Court decisions dismissing his motions to stay a Canadian Judicial Council inquiry.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Federal Court struck the appellant's judicial review applications, and this Court dismissed his appeals as premature in Dugré #1.

citations.why: Reports this Court's dismissal of appellant's appeals as premature

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Attorney General argues the appeals should be dismissed as there is no main proceeding justifying the stay motions, and the motions lack serious issues and other stay criteria.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Court invited written submissions on whether the appeals are doomed to fail following Dugré #1 and should be summarily dismissed.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The appellant seeks a stay of the appeals pending Supreme Court leave or decision on Dugré #1; the Attorney General opposes this request.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court refuses to stay the appeals due to procedural problems caused by multiple interlocutory proceedings, citing Dugré #1 and C.B. Powell.
idea_list: Cites procedural problems and precedent C.B. Powell

citations.why: Supports refusal to stay due to procedural issues

citations.cite: Canada (Border Services Agency) v. C.B. Powell Limited, 2010 FCA 61, [2011] 2 F.C.R. 332 [C.B. Powell] at paras. 30-32
citations.why: Cited for principle of non-interference and procedural congestion

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court explains that procedural congestion and paralysis justify the non-interference principle from C.B. Powell, which should be fully considered.

citations.why: Explains non-interference principle to avoid procedural paralysis

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Following Dugré #1, no main proceeding justifies the stay motions, so the appeals are doomed to fail and should be dismissed.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court dismisses the appeals and proposes no costs since the Attorney General did not seek them.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The reasons will be filed in docket A-118-20 and copies in A-119-20 and A-120-20; the decision is signed by the Chief Justice and two judges.
